newsitem.title: CANADA: Police name dead British cable car victim.
newsitem.headline: Police name dead British cable car victim.

text.p: A 47-year-old British woman killed in a cable car crash in historic Quebec City was identified by police on Sunday as Helen Christine Tombs from London.
Another British woman was still in critical condition on Sunday, police spokesman Capt. Michel Golaneck said. Her name was not released.
Tombs died from internal injuries suffered in Saturday's accident, police said.

The cable car, which spans part of the former garrison city, fell from a height of 20-25 feet (6-7 metres), injuring 16 tourists. Four were from Britain, four from Canada's Quebec province and the others from the Unitied States -- six from Massachusetts, one from Ohio and one from New Hampshire.
The tourists were aged between 31 and 74, Golaneck said.

The year-round funicular railway descends from the Chateau Frontenac hotel high above the St. Lawrence river to a lower part of Quebec's capital city. At about 1550 EST (1950 GMT) on Saturday a cable snapped, hurtling the car against a wall of a booth and shattering the windows, with the 16 tourists inside.
The cable car ride, which lasts roughly a minute, is a popular tourist attraction.
